blockers.title: The authorization-record re-scope leaves consentCarrier without a doctor-v4 destination and breaks the mapping's 19/19 totality rule
evidence: doctorV4FieldMapping.rule requires a destination for every one of the 19 authorizationRecord members and says key-set equality alone is insufficient; a member with no destination is a contract defect.

The new destinations.consentCarrier value points back to authorizationRecord.consentCarrier and explains its discriminator role. It names no consentRecords[] destination or structured encoding. consentCarrier is intentionally absent from the closed 15-member scope and from doctor v4's 13 consent-record members; residualLimitation is expressly not a substitute.

The null/object policyProvenance union could encode the two carrier values bijectively, but destinations.consentCarrier never declares that encoding. Counting a source self-reference as the nineteenth destination contradicts the mapping rule's own key-set-is-not-sufficient warning.

The new appliesTo entry also names authorizationRecord.closedMembers[policyProvenance] nullWhen/requiredWhen, but that record member has no nullWhen or requiredWhen keys; it has only prose semantics plus type/union/whenPresent. The record-side machine link therefore points to predicates that do not exist.
The subject's own predecessor history records HAE3-CX-01 as repaired at doctorV4FieldMapping 19/19 destinations and FC-ROUND-TRIP; v12 reopens that invariant while retaining mappedMemberCount 19.
blockers.impact: FC-CARRIER-SHAPE is now decidable before projection, so IR-HEA10-B1's original fixture defect is addressed. But the contract still promises a total authorization-record-to-doctor mapping and cannot account for one source member after projection. An implementation must either drop consentCarrier without the declared encoding, treat a source field as its own destination, or silently infer an unstated round-trip rule. That is a load-bearing mapping-totality failure.
blockers.requiredRepair: Declare the structured doctor-side encoding for consentCarrier, for example that consentRecords[].scope.policyProvenance null reconstructs invocation-time-naming and a well-formed object reconstructs pre-existing-policy, and test that round trip; alternatively revise the mapping rule/count to explicitly classify consentCarrier as a consumed validation-only discriminator without falsely calling it a destination. Add literal record-side nullWhen/requiredWhen predicates or make appliesTo target constraints that actually exist.
